additional_requirements: depressive_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness (Criterion C)
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode (Criterion B)

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

info.persona: Johnny Renelus, a pragmatic yet curious 62‑year‑old forklift veteran, balances a competitive drive with a skeptical eye, turning every woodworking project, fishing outing, and vintage truck restoration into a disciplined test of skill—though they habitually check their blood pressure before coffee and hoard spare parts they never use.
info.professional_persona: Johnny Renelus, a seasoned industrial truck and tractor operator with 35 years of hands‑on expertise, blends meticulous load‑handling precision and a safety‑first mindset with a pragmatic curiosity for emerging automation, while they mentor newcomers with a competitive edge and a healthy dose of measured skepticism.
info.cultural_background: Johnny is a second‑generation African American born and raised in Cincinnati’s Avondale neighborhood. His grandparents migrated north during the Great Migration, bringing Southern culinary traditions, gospel music, and a strong sense of community resilience. He grew up immersed in church life, where church service, soul food, and storytelling shaped his values of hard work, mutual support, and perseverance. His cultural identity informs his respectful yet competitive approach at work, his dedication to mentoring younger Black workers, and his pride in preserving African‑American culinary and musical heritage through family gatherings and local events.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Johnny enjoys woodworking projects that let him blend practical skill with creative problem‑solving, often building custom furniture for his family. He is an enthusiastic fisherman, frequenting the Ohio River and nearby lakes for quiet reflection. His love of music includes gospel choirs at his local church and classic soul records, which he shares during community gatherings. He also follows classic car shows, occasionally helping to restore a vintage truck in his garage. Reading historical biographies and attending local cultural festivals keep his curiosity alive while providing a balanced social outlet.
info.sports_persona: Johnny Renelus, a devoted fan of the Cincinnati Bengals and the Cincinnati Reds, spends their evenings fishing on the Ohio River while they maintain a steady fitness regimen of sunrise walks and a weekly senior bowling league at the local YMCA, balancing their competitive spirit with a relaxed, low‑impact approach to staying active.
info.arts_persona: Johnny Renelus finds artistic fulfillment in the resonant harmonies of the St. Mary’s gospel choir and the timeless soul of Aretha Franklin, Marvin Gaye, and Sam Cooke, often sharing these classics at community potlucks, while they channel their appreciation for vintage automotive aesthetics into participation at classic car shows featuring restored 1950s trucks.
info.travel_persona: Johnny Renelus plans their travel with meticulous spreadsheets, favoring relaxed road trips along the Great River Road to historic river towns such as Louisville and Natchez, while they dream of a future cultural pilgrimage to European heritage sites like Stratford‑upon‑Avon and the Musée du Quai Branly in Paris, balancing their modest retirement budget with a desire for meaningful historical immersion.
info.culinary_persona: Johnny Renelus enjoys cooking hearty Midwestern comfort fare, often preparing their signature Cincinnati chili with a secret blend of spices, ground beef, kidney beans, and Worcestershire sauce, while their fishing trips inspire pan‑seared trout seasoned with lemon, dill, and garlic, showcasing their competent home‑cook skills that blend tradition with a touch of culinary experimentation.

info.persona: Stacey Wilson channels a curiosity‑driven, art‑loving hustle into a flexible, people‑centric career, balancing spontaneous brunches, occasional financial slip‑ups, and a habit of leaving coffee cups on the kitchen counter.
info.professional_persona: Stacey Wilson, a 27‑year‑old business operations specialist in northern Alabama, blends keen analytical skills in Excel, PowerBI, and NetSuite with a vibrant artistic sensibility, turning process‑improvement projects into collaborative, culture‑rich experiences that energize stakeholders and drive efficiency.
info.cultural_background: Stacey grew up in Arab, Alabama, a small town steeped in Southern hospitality and close‑knit community values. Raised in a middle‑class, white family with strong ties to church and local traditions, she learned the importance of courtesy, modesty, and helping neighbors. The region’s emphasis on storytelling, music, and communal gatherings nurtured her sociable, talkative personality and her appreciation for varied cultural experiences. While grounded in Southern customs—such as a love for home‑cooked meals, outdoor gatherings, and community festivals—Stacey also embraces broader artistic and innovative influences, blending her regional roots with a curiosity for new ideas and unconventional thinking.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her downtime Stacey immerses herself in the vibrant arts scene of northern Alabama—visiting local galleries, sketching watercolors of the rolling hills, and attending community theater productions. She loves spontaneous weekend road trips to explore new coffee shops, music festivals, and historic towns. Cooking Southern comfort food, especially experimenting with modern twists on classic recipes, is a favorite way to host friends and family. Stacey also enjoys yoga, hiking the nearby Oak Mountain trails, and volunteering at youth art programs, where she mentors kids in using creativity for problem‑solving. Her talkative, sociable side shines when she organizes brunch gatherings and city‑wide networking mixers for professionals interested in blending business and creativity.
info.sports_persona: Stacey Wilson fuels their love of the outdoors with weekly hikes on Oak Mountain and sunrise yoga, joins the local trail club for seasonal 5K runs, and roots for the Alabama Crimson Tide during football season while cheering on the Birmingham Barons on summer evenings.
info.arts_persona: Stacey Wilson immerses themselves in the northern Alabama arts scene, sketching watercolors of rolling hills after attending exhibitions featuring works by regional painter Mary Ann Sampson, catching performances by the local community theater's rendition of "Our Town", and curating playlists that blend Jason Isbell's folk‑rock with the abstract pop of Andy Warhol.
info.travel_persona: Stacey Wilson prefers spontaneous, road‑trip‑driven getaways, charting weekend routes to Asheville’s craft‑brew scene, the historic streets of Savannah, and the eclectic art installations of Marfa, Texas, while budgeting carefully to keep their dream of a summer bike tour along the Blue Ridge Parkway within reach.
info.culinary_persona: Stacey Wilson, an adept home chef, reimagines Southern comfort foods by pairing classic shrimp and grits with a miso glaze, perfecting fried green tomatoes topped with bourbon‑infused hot honey, and crafting pecan pie with a dash of smoked paprika, all while hosting lively brunches that showcase farm‑to‑table ingredients like heirloom tomatoes and fresh basil.

info.persona: Robert Maldonado, a 30-year-old customer support professional, blends methodical precision with an art-infused curiosity, juggling a spreadsheet-driven budget, midnight ramen cravings, and a habit of documenting every coffee brew in a leather-bound journal; they thrive on quiet evenings spent sketching cityscapes.
info.professional_persona: Robert Maldonado, a 30-year-old customer support specialist, leverages his methodical mindset, empathetic problem solving, and eye for design to streamline Zendesk workflows while regularly offering UI/UX feedback that reflects his curiosity and appreciation for visual art; they seek to transition into a team lead role within three years.
info.cultural_background: Robert grew up in Northridge, a multicultural suburb of Los Angeles, as part of a White Hispanic family with roots in Mexico. His parents blended Anglo‑American middle‑class values with Mexican traditions, celebrating holidays such as Thanksgiving and Christmas alongside Dia de los Muertos and Cinco de Mayo. Bilingual in English and conversational Spanish, he was exposed to a rich tapestry of music, cuisine, and community events that fostered his appreciation for diverse artistic expression. This bicultural upbringing reinforced a strong work ethic, respect for harmony, and an open‑minded curiosity that continues to shape his personal and professional life.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his free time, Robert explores contemporary art galleries and museum exhibitions in Los Angeles, often sketching scenes in a small notebook. He enjoys photography, focusing on urban street photography and nature shots during hikes in the Santa Monica Mountains. His curiosity drives him to read a mix of modern philosophy, science fiction, and non‑fiction books about emerging technologies. He frequents independent coffee shops, trying new brewing methods, and practices journaling to reflect on ideas and plan personal projects. Occasionally, he plays strategy board games with a close circle of friends and attends local indie film screenings and live jazz performances.
info.sports_persona: Robert Maldonado follows the Los Angeles Lakers and Dodgers avidly, joins the Santa Monica Hiking Club for weekly trail runs, and squeezes in pick-up basketball at his neighborhood gym, balancing his love for outdoor endurance with modest strength training; they consider Saturday morning jogs essential for mental clarity.
info.arts_persona: Robert Maldonado spends weekends sketching at LACMA, curating his Instagram feed with street shots reminiscent of Henri Cartier-Bresson, attends live jazz sets by Kamasi Washington, and enjoys contemporary installations by Yayoi Kusama, all of which feed his creative mindset; they often journal about how colors influence user experience design.
info.travel_persona: Robert Maldonado carefully maps his trips in a spreadsheet, favoring week-long cultural immersion journeys like the Day of the Dead festivals in Oaxaca and the art districts of Tokyo, while weekend hikes in Yosemite satisfy his love for nature, and a looming budget keeps his future dream of Patagonia’s glaciers on hold; they prefer solo travel but occasionally invite a close friend along for city tours.
info.culinary_persona: Robert Maldonado, an avid home-cook, perfects avocado-lime salsa and grilled fish tacos with roasted corn, experiments with pour-over coffee using Ethiopian beans, and rarely forgoes the occasional mole poblano when his friends gather, though his midnight snack habit of instant ramen remains a guilty pleasure; they keep a small herb garden on the balcony to harvest fresh cilantro.
